newsitem.title: USA: Safety board starts hearing on Valujet crash.
newsitem.headline: Safety board starts hearing on Valujet crash.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board was meeting Tuesday to consider its final report on the crash last year of ValuJet flight 592 that killed 110 people.

The DC-9 plunged into the Florida Everglades on May 11, 1996. Preliminary reports show the crash was caused by a fire in the cargo hold fueled by oxygen-generating canisters that were improperly handled and labeled.

In a statement prepared for the NTSB meeting, investigator-in-charge, Gregory Feith, said that of the 25 oxygen generators found at the accident site, many of them bore internal and external evidence of fire and heat damage.
An agenda for the meeting listed the role of ValuJet and its contractor, SabreTech Corp., in the accident as well as the oversight of the Federal Aviation Administration as matters for consideration.

Feith said employees at SabreTech were told to clean up their facility before a potential customer made an inspection. As part of that cleanup, 144 oxygen generators were packed into five boxes and put aboard flight 592 marked as company material and listed on the manifest as "oxy cannisters - empty."
ValuJet is to merge shortly with AirWays Corp. and will be renamed AirTran Airlines.
